title: Hotline 1.9 protocol documentation gap register
method: Documentation review, native Ghidra/source analysis and portable paired packet corpora. Added24 final banner observations for GIF, URL/absence controls, selectors, cancellation, replacement and bounded expiry; failed setup/restoration probes retained. Other image formats, absent-buffer recovery, full operation/peer coverage and Kani completion remain unclaimed.

gaps.title: Define the supported 1.9 subset

sources.heading: Hotline Server Protocol 1.9: Transactions and Functionality Guide
Open compatibility gaps and QA requirements

gaps.question: Which of the 45 requests and server notifications must mxd implement now, defer explicitly, or reject, and which peer profiles are acceptance targets?
gaps.implementation_impact: An open-ended baseline cannot define feature completion or compatible rejection behaviour.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish an operation-by-profile scope matrix with required, deferred and excluded states, including replies to unsupported operations.

gaps.title: Canonical transaction and field schemas
gaps.question: For every in-scope request, reply and notification, which fields are required, optional, conditional or repeatable, with what widths and value domains?
gaps.implementation_impact: Lists of fields that a handler reads are not sufficient to build a compatible encoder or validator.
gaps.closure_criteria: Provide a schema registry for the core operations, marking each remaining unknown with a gap ID; include direction, cardinality, width, conditions and defaults.

resolution.closure: Published a core operation registry with direction, logical scalar/repeated occurrence, widths/byte caps, default/absence behaviour and conditions. Remaining type, boundary, routing and fixture unknowns retain their separate gap IDs as required by this criterion. This closes the registry deliverable, not all codec/runtime acceptance questions.

gaps.title: Error-code and failure-outcome registry
gaps.question: Which statuses, field-100 forms and connection outcomes apply to each failure, including errors in operations without a normal ACK?
gaps.implementation_impact: Implementations cannot distinguish recoverable failure, success, silent rejection and impending disconnect consistently.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document a failure table and representative bytes for authentication, permission, missing-object, malformed-request and unsupported-operation cases.

resolution.progress: Captured the108-entry native-result table, verified sorted keys and documented representative internal domain/code mappings with resource meanings. These are not wire statuses; enclosing catch translation and native error packets remain required. Retained native status1 authentication, permission, missing room/file and unknown/replayed-operation replies, plus invalid zero-size closure. Internal exception translation and remaining failure/drain boundaries remain unresolved.
resolution.closure: Not closed: remaining unchanged acceptance requirements are explicitly retained above.

gaps.title: Transaction ID lifecycle and correlation
gaps.question: Are zero, duplicate, wrapped or reused IDs accepted, how are client and server ID spaces separated, and how are unsolicited replies treated?
gaps.implementation_impact: Correlation and reassembly can attach a reply or payload to the wrong outstanding operation.
gaps.closure_criteria: Specify ID allocation, lifetime, wrap/reuse and notification correlation rules; exercise zero, collision and late-reply cases.

resolution.progress: Recorded per-connection increment/zero-skipping wrap and fragment matching. Collision, reuse and late-reply fixtures remain required. Short41/wrongmagic/wrongversion RFLT records produce no reply10 observed before3secondpause and subsequent500ACK. Initial30secondwait is preserved as timeout, not numberederror evidence. Missing/completed uploadresume returnsstatus1+message100 withoutref. Full failure cataloguemapping remains required.
resolution.closure: Not closed: broader unchanged acceptance requirements remain as stated above.

gaps.title: Connection timers and liveness

sources.heading: Additional Observed Requests and Scope Gaps

gaps.question: What are the handshake, login, agreement, idle and partial-frame deadlines, and what traffic resets them?
gaps.implementation_impact: A client can wait forever or disconnect a compatible session prematurely without a liveness contract.
gaps.closure_criteria: Provide a timer/state table with units, reset conditions, configurable values and close outcomes, distinguishing native observations from mxd limits.

resolution.progress: Published timer origins/reset conditions: only selected logical requests refresh session activity; upload entry clocks begin at request creation and attachment does not reset them; consumed file chunks refresh them. Added bounded pending/partial-input negatives and late-attachment derived case. Lower-layer/configured timing and native boundary fixtures remain required. Guest trace establishes no FIN/RST during65.060281 host seconds after a failed-login reply before client cleanup. A separate isolated35-second quiet case resets the failed session92.254ms after a new control SYN. Added primary OT predicate/close helper captures. Dispatcher scheduling, guard semantics across profiles and clock/configuration boundaries remain open; no hard30-second deadline is claimed.
resolution.closure: Not closed: the remaining unchanged acceptance requirements are explicitly retained above.

gaps.title: Complete direction and reply-contract catalogue

sources.heading: Sending a Chat Message (Transaction 105) – Client Initiates
Leaving a Chat Room (Transaction 116) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: Which operation/direction/session-state combinations are accepted, and what direct success/error replies or subsequent notifications belong to each? The current ACK/Push prose is not a complete catalogue.
gaps.implementation_impact: Implementers must infer dispatch direction and negative-outcome rules from scattered handler descriptions rather than one complete contract.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish an operation-by-direction/state table distinguishing direct success replies, error replies, emitted notifications and acceptance/completion semantics.

resolution.closure: Published all45 explicit request paths with direction/state eligibility, direct success and explicit-error outcomes, fan-out ordering and acceptance/completion semantics. This satisfies the unchanged table criterion. Exhaustive exception translation and runtime capture requirements remain GAP-003/084; the former is not a prerequisite of this static catalogue.

gaps.title: Allowed operations by session state

sources.heading: Additional Observed Requests and Scope Gaps

gaps.question: What can be sent before authentication, after login ACK, while agreement is pending, after early completion and during shutdown?
gaps.implementation_impact: The guide has transaction descriptions but no complete dispatch/state contract for a server implementation.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish a state/operation table including invalid transitions, replayed login/agreement requests and state-specific failures, backed by traces or dispatcher analysis.

resolution.closure: Published allowed operations, invalid pre-online closes, replayed online login/agreement errors, failure waiting and disconnected teardown states, backed by dispatcher analysis as allowed by the closure criterion. Removed the planned GAP-025 prerequisite because dispatch was established directly; full configured sequence captures remain GAP-025/084.

gaps.title: Handshake failures and stream boundaries
gaps.question: How are short, long, pipelined, wrong-magic, wrong-version or unsupported-sub-version handshakes consumed, replied to and closed?
gaps.implementation_impact: The happy-path twelve/eight-byte layouts do not specify initial stream recovery or rejection.
gaps.closure_criteria: Record positive and negative handshake exchanges with exact byte consumption, response status, pipelining behaviour and closure order.

resolution.closure: Recorded positive and negative primary handshake exchanges, exact12-byte/prefix preservation, five3-second split observations, short-input half-close, pipelined login and failure response/guest RST-versus-FIN order. Fourteen addressed final cases include13 completed plans and an explicitly failed alternate-control probe. The unchanged ordinary handshake criterion is met; alternate wrapping, matched HTXF streams, scheduling and identified peers remain GAP-009/010/005/055/080/084.

gaps.title: Sub-version 3 and direct HTXF relationship
gaps.question: When does the TRTP sub-version-3 path apply, on which endpoint, and how does it relate to a direct sixteen-byte HTXF header?
gaps.implementation_impact: An implementer could perform the wrong handshake on a transfer socket despite knowing each observed magic.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace the two entry paths and document complete endpoint-specific sequences, transitions and fixture bytes.

resolution.closure: Both raw5501 and primarycontrol5500 TRTPv1sub3 entry paths have positive matched-reference upload/download sequences with exact host/guest packet reconciliation. The handover success is read before same-connectionHTXF. Earlier native-transport-01 retains unmatched ref0 negatives through both entry paths. Completion boundaries are direction-specific: uploadEOF versus downloadadvertisedcount with open transport and explicit214 cleanup. Alternate5502/5503 wrapping remainsGAP-010, banner matchingGAP-055 and full peersGAP-084.

gaps.title: Listening endpoints and data-port arithmetic
gaps.question: How are control/data listeners selected and configured, and is the data port always the base port plus one in this build?
gaps.implementation_impact: File-transfer connection setup cannot be derived from a tentative port convention.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace listener creation and configuration; document endpoint mapping, exceptions and verified client connection examples.

resolution.progress: Traced configured base port (default 5500), ordinary base/base+1 and alternative-wrapper base+2/base+3 binds. Constructor modes are kept separate from unproven TLS/HTTP labels. Runtime/overflow/client connection fixtures remain required. Native primary control5500 and data5501 examples retained. Alternate5502/5503 accept TCP and acknowledge unwrapped input but return no application response within10 seconds; full wrapping and port-boundary/overflow configuration remain unverified.
resolution.closure: Not closed: the remaining unchanged acceptance requirements are explicitly retained above.

gaps.title: Frame, transaction and buffering limits
gaps.question: Is the image's 2 MiB value changed at runtime, does it bound a frame or aggregate transaction, and how are totals, fragments and concurrent buffers limited?
gaps.implementation_impact: The existing image constant does not define safe or interoperable allocation and framing boundaries.
gaps.closure_criteria: Document native comparisons/configuration and explicit mxd limits with inclusive boundaries, overflow checks and boundary fixtures.

resolution.progress: Captured explicit startup assignment of 512 KiB to receive-limit global, superseding the image-only 2 MiB assumption for that path. Indirect future writes, configurability, aggregate bounds and boundary fixtures remain required. Native boundary cases confirm zero/above512KiB size words close, equality524288 passes and aggregate524290 can dispatch. mxd limits, configuration/write paths and global buffering bounds remain required.
resolution.closure: Not closed: broader unchanged acceptance requirements remain as stated above.

gaps.title: Fragment reassembly edge cases
gaps.question: What happens when type/total changes, fragments interleave, lengths overrun or underfill, transactions are abandoned, or a partial frame ends in EOF?
gaps.implementation_impact: A codec implementing only ordinary concatenation has no specified outcome for common malformed or interrupted input.
gaps.closure_criteria: Publish reassembly invariants and a test matrix covering keys, length consistency, overshoot, underflow, abandonment and partial TCP delivery.

resolution.progress: Complete-request selection requires accumulated length at least total; partial TCP/frame/fragment progress does not update dispatcher activity in traced paths. No assembly-age check is established there. Native collision/abandonment and buffering fixtures remain required. Captured total/type replacement, overshoot, interleaved IDs, abandoned-partial coexistence, request/reply namespace separation, sequentialIDreuse and incompleteTCP silence. Assembly age, collision lifecycle and global buffering remain unproven.
resolution.closure: Not closed: broader unchanged acceptance requirements remain as stated above.

gaps.title: Accepted envelope values and reserved bytes
gaps.question: How are nonzero flags, reply markers other than zero/one, nonzero request error words, unsupported types and nonzero reply types handled?
gaps.implementation_impact: Writer conventions do not define the input-validation contract.
gaps.closure_criteria: Specify accepted and rejected header values for each direction and their failure outcomes, supported by receiver checks and negative fixtures.

resolution.progress: Documented nonzero reply-byte discrimination and lack of a flags whitelist in the traced receiver. Full direction-specific negative fixtures remain required. Captured flagsff, errorwordffffffff, requestIDzero and unmatched reply bytes1/2/255, plus size rejection closes. Full direction-specific accepted/rejected envelope policy remains required.
resolution.closure: Not closed: broader unchanged acceptance requirements remain as stated above.

gaps.title: TLV structural validation
gaps.question: What happens with a missing count, count/length mismatch, truncated values, trailing bytes, zero field IDs, unknown fields or maximum field counts?
gaps.implementation_impact: The record shape alone is insufficient for a deterministic parameter decoder.
gaps.closure_criteria: Define exact consumption, bounds, unknown-field and trailing-data rules; add byte fixtures at every boundary and mismatch class.

resolution.closure: Exact prefix consumption, record/header/value bounds, unknown/zero IDs and trailing-data rules are defined with retained helper code and native boundary/mismatch fixtures. Settings304 outcomes independently expose complete indexed values and defaults. Other handlers may reject those defaults; their transaction-specific acceptance remains separate.

gaps.title: Field-specific scalar types
gaps.question: Which numeric fields permit one/two/four bytes, which are fixed-width or signed, and how are booleans, sentinel values and invalid widths interpreted?
gaps.implementation_impact: The generic reader's three-byte-to-zero behaviour could be mistaken for a valid zero or applied to a fixed-width field.
gaps.closure_criteria: Give each core scalar an explicit wire type, allowed widths/range and invalid-width outcome, including references and privilege bitmaps.

resolution.progress: Core registry now supplies field-specific scalar/byte/bitmap/record schemas. Non-core types and malformed-width/range native fixtures remain required. Captured settings icon widths0..5, low16bit narrowing and301 signed-short promotion:8000 emitsffff8000; initial wrong hypothesis retained. Other core scalar/reference/bitmap malformed-width outcomes remain required.
resolution.closure: Not closed: broader unchanged acceptance requirements remain as stated above.

gaps.title: Absent, empty and zero-valued fields
gaps.question: Which operations distinguish an omitted field, a zero-length TLV, an empty string and numeric zero, and what defaults are applied?
gaps.implementation_impact: The native writer omits empty fields while documented readers sometimes reset state when fields are absent.
gaps.closure_criteria: Add per-field presence/default tables and fixtures for all four cases, especially credentials, settings and partial account updates.

resolution.progress: Account and session settings presence/default tables are published, including missing/empty/NUL password and comment distinctions. Other operations and full native fixture coverage remain required.
resolution.closure: Not closed: remaining acceptance evidence is listed above.

gaps.title: Repeated scalar fields and ordering
gaps.question: Beyond observed list/invitation cases, are duplicate scalars rejected, first-wins, last-wins or accumulated, and is order meaningful?
gaps.implementation_impact: Preserving repetitions is necessary but does not determine how each schema resolves ambiguous duplicates.
gaps.closure_criteria: Define multiplicity and ordering by transaction/field and test repeated scalars, interleaved repeated records and reordered inputs.

resolution.progress: Established sorted binary-search scalar selection without a first/last guarantee and original-order indexed iteration. Duplicate/reorder fixtures remain required. Four duplicate icon orders emitted the last icon in those cases only. Interleaved repeated-record and transaction/field multiplicity coverage remain incomplete; no universal last-wins policy inferred.
resolution.closure: Not closed: broader unchanged acceptance requirements remain as stated above.

gaps.title: ACK versus completion, durability and retry

Posting a News Article (Transaction 410) – Client Initiates

gaps.question: When an ACK precedes routing or mutation side effects, what has it committed to, and what can fail or be retried afterwards?
gaps.implementation_impact: A client may treat acceptance as delivered/durable success and duplicate non-idempotent operations on reconnect.
gaps.closure_criteria: Specify completion points, post-ACK failure signalling, persistence and retry/idempotency rules per operation with disconnect-boundary fixtures.

resolution.progress: Added news structure order: Trash move or directory/category creation precedes ACK; creation activity logging follows ACK. INFO FlushVol return is unchecked. Disconnect-boundary, persistence, retry/idempotency and postACK failure fixtures remain required.

gaps.title: Native nonempty-password encoding

gaps.implementation_impact: The guide cannot yet supply a working nonempty-password authentication fixture.
gaps.closure_criteria: Trace account storage and comparisons, then capture successful and failed logins plus account changes using known nonempty credentials.

resolution.closure: Native setter/storage/comparison tracing is now joined by successful login with a created known nonempty password, network password change, acceptance of the replacement, rejection of the old password and plaintext replacement bytes, and the matching734-byte stored account record. This satisfies the unchanged credential criterion. Length extremes, restart durability, encoding policy and transport close timing remain GAP-019/064/072/082/084.
